description: The configuration surface of the haproxy chart. GENERATED from values.yaml by `./build.sh Charts` and diffed in CI — docs/plan/03 § charts/. Edit values.yaml, never this file. Members carrying `x-cybercloud-api: false` are chart or platform plumbing and are not part of the resource body.

addresses.description: The workload addresses to balance across, comma separated — for example 10.20.1.11,10.20.1.12. ⚠ Addresses and not resource ids: there is no service discovery and no DNS inside a virtual network, so an address is what a tenant has for their own workloads. At most 32.

port.description: The TCP port every backend address is reached on. ⚠ One port for the whole pool: a pool whose members listen on different ports is two pools.

frontend.description: The address and port workloads connect to.

port.description: The TCP port the proxy listens on. ⚠ There is no protocol setting: HAProxy does not proxy UDP in any version, so every rule here is TCP.

v4.description: The IPv4 address the proxy answers on, inside the subnet's range. ⚠ Required, and it is the one thing about this resource a tenant must choose: there is no DNS inside a virtual network, so an address nobody picked is an address nothing can be pointed at. A bare address and never a prefix.

v6.description: The IPv6 address the proxy also answers on, or empty. ⚠ Lower case only, for the fabric's reason. It must be inside the subnet's IPv6 range, which means the subnet has to have one.

health.description: How a backend is decided to be up. ⚠ Checking cannot be turned off — a proxy that sends connections to a dead server is worse than no proxy.

healthyAfter.description: How many successful probes put a backend back into the pool.

intervalSeconds.description: How often each backend is probed with a TCP connection.

unhealthyAfter.description: How many failed probes take a backend out of the pool.

imageRepository.description: Where the HAProxy image is pulled from.
imageRepository.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Docker's own library/haproxy, unmodified. A tenant choosing what runs in a pod on their own subnet is not a configuration surface, and a mirror is an operator's decision rather than a tenant's.

limits.description: What the proxy refuses rather than passes on.

maxConnections.description: How many connections the frontend accepts at once. ⚠ Further connections wait in the kernel's accept queue rather than being refused, so this is a back-pressure setting rather than a firewall. It is also applied per backend server.

nameOverride.description: Replace the generated object-name stem. Empty means derive it from the release name.
nameOverride.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Helm plumbing. Nothing about it belongs in a resource body.

platform.description: Resource identity injected by the reconciler. Not a tenant-facing setting.

apiVersion.description: The api-version the resource was last written at, rendered into the cybercloud.io/api-version label.
apiVersion.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

managedBy.description: Value of the cybercloud.io/managed-by label. Constant, and the selector every informer filters on.
managedBy.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

namespace.description: The resource's own namespace, which is the first component of that same Subnet object's name.
namespace.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

resourceGroup.description: Resource group name, rendered into the cybercloud.io/resource-group label.
resourceGroup.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

resourceId.description: Resource GUID, rendered into the cybercloud.io/resource-id label.
resourceId.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

resourceType.description: Fully qualified resource type, rendered into the cybercloud.io/resource-type label.
resourceType.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

subscriptionId.description: Subscription GUID, rendered into the cybercloud.io/subscription-id label.
subscriptionId.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

tenantId.description: Tenant GUID, rendered into the cybercloud.io/tenant-id label.
tenantId.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

virtualNetwork.description: The parent virtual network's name, which is a component of the Subnet object the proxy pod is annotated onto.
virtualNetwork.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

platform.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

sizing.description: CPU and memory for the proxy.

preset.description: How much the proxy pod gets. An L4 proxy is mostly kernel work, so the small row carries far more than its size suggests; the larger rows are for many long-lived connections.

subnet.description: The subnet of this virtual network the proxy sits on. ⚠ The proxy gets an address from it, so the frontend address below must be inside its range. A name that is not a subnet of this network is refused by the fabric rather than by the API, and the proxy pod never schedules.

version.description: Which HAProxy line to run. 3.2 is the long-term-support line and is the default; 3.4 is the current one. ⚠ A change here restarts the proxy and drops open connections.
